answer: Sybil resistance is better priced than policed. Charge a rising registration bond instead of a flat fee: a new key posts more collateral as more identities trace to the same funding source, so a second account is cheap and the twentieth is not. The kernel is that price attaches to the cluster, not the account: a farm pays the integral of the curve, not one fee repeated. Extra identities become as dear as saffron to an attacker; a lone operator barely notices. Each account grafted onto the same vine needs its own bond and attestations, so a fake persona costs as much as a real one, then more.
